verses.text: The people of the land made Josiah’s son Jehoahaz king in his father’s place in Jerusalem.
Joahaz was twenty-three when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for three months.
The king of Egypt removed him from power in Jerusalem and fined the land a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
The king of Egypt made Joahaz’s brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Joahaz away to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. He did evil in the sight of the LORD his God.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came against him and shackled him to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the vessels from the LORD’s house to Babylon and put them in his own temple there.
The rest of Jehoiakim’s acts, the detestable things he did, and what was found in him are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for three months and ten days. He did evil in the LORD’s sight.

At the turn of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon along with the valuable vessels from the LORD’s house. He made Jehoiachin’s brother Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years.
He did evil in the sight of the LORD his God. He refused to humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke the LORD’s own words.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God. Zedekiah grew stubborn, hardened his heart, and refused to turn to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The leading priests and the people also went deep into wrongdoing, following all the detestable practices of the nations. They defiled the house the LORD had made holy in Jerusalem.
The LORD, the God of their ancestors, got up early to send them word through his messengers. He had compassion for his people and for his dwelling place.
But they mocked God’s messengers, brushed off his words with contempt, and laughed at his prophets until the LORD’s anger rose against his people and there was no remedy left.

So the LORD brought the king of the Chaldeans against them. He killed their young men with the sword right inside their sanctuary. He spared no one out of pity, whether young man or young woman, old or frail. The LORD handed them all over to him.
The king took everything to Babylon, the vessels from God’s house, big and small, the treasures of the LORD’s house, and the treasures of the king and his officials.
They burned God’s house, tore down Jerusalem’s wall, set all its palaces on fire, and destroyed all its valuables.
He took the people who escaped the sword into exile in Babylon. They served him and his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power.
That fulfilled what the LORD had said through Jeremiah. The land got its Sabbath rests. All the time it lay deserted, it kept Sabbath until the seventy years were complete.

In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia, the LORD stirred up Cyrus’s spirit to fulfill the word he’d spoken through Jeremiah. Cyrus sent out a proclamation across his whole kingdom and put it in writing:

“Here’s what Cyrus, king of Persia, says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He’s commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem in Judah. If any of you belong to his people, may the LORD your God be with you. Go on up.’”
